correctness.rationale: For all k>=4, the companion matrix satisfies M^8=I+4D and D_s stabilization. Direct residues of eM^nD_3v for even n and eM^nD_4v for n=1,3 mod8 prove exact index-isometry valuations. The two critical branches have rigorously integral restricted power-series remainders divisible by eight after their explicit quadratic terms. Contraction gives unique critical points, their Taylor unit factors are 1 mod8 and admit Lipschitz square roots, hence each branch is exactly conjugate by an isometry to the square map. Index count weights follow from least period 2^{k+1}. The explicit square-root formula includes zero and all small exponents. Independent matrix and enumeration checker passed k=4..14. No infinite assertion rests on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The closest complete primary manuscript (2026 dyadic-image theorem) explicitly withholds per-residue multiplicities in its limitations: it gives the set of values, not individual preimage counts. The new theorem adds the exact r=7 critical square conjugacy, r=1 and r=3 nonsingular preimage weights, and their joint all-target formula. Bilu et al. 2022 and Marques-Lengyel 2014 treat valuations/zeros rather than arbitrary target counts; Klaska 2008 treats primitive period lengths. Target-to-target multiplicity is not logically implied by a set of attained residues or a period alone.

value.rationale: Residue image support and period are insufficient to answer exact frequency of an individual target. A fully explicit distribution of all two-adic preimages is a natural refinement with arithmetic content: branch weights, two critical square-map singularities, unbounded collision sizes, and a closed root-count formula for every k and y. The r=7 critical geometry and residue-wise counts are a structurally new invariant, not a special numerical recomputation.
